ideas.title: You are the weather
ideas.critique: This is round 1's Whirlwind handed to the player, and a WASD mini game is the second in ten posts, so the form is already worn. What's strong is that the vortex physics is new, and being the thing that throws props and leaves them where they land gives a messy island you'd want to come back and wreck again. Friends grumbling home is the scripted one-liner part.

ideas.title: Jelly day
ideas.critique: It's one more 'the whole ground does something to everyone' day after the seesaw and the sand. But a real wave equation that carries trees, props and bodies and launches them far away is a new way things move, and you can play it. If the friends 'jumping on purpose' turns into a scripted gag loop instead of the waves really launching them, most of the value is lost.

ideas.title: Gravity takes a minute off
ideas.critique: Things falling and bouncing is an example the goals already name, and a one-minute island-wide event that ends in a crash leaves nothing to play with afterwards. A floating ball of water and a slow cloud of sand grains are the only pictures here that would be new.

ideas.title: Swallowed
ideas.critique: This is a scripted set piece with a new creature, a story beat and a hiccup punchline, so you watch it once and you're done. Sunlight glowing through subsurface-scattering skin is real path-tracer material, but it's a still-life wrapped in a story, not anything that moves or plays differently.

ideas.title: Island dominoes
ideas.critique: Toppling is the 'things that fall' example from the goals, and friends lining up the island's props is another gathering that makes an arrangement. Tipping physics that runs over a whole route, through the hill and the bridge, has a satisfying chase. Whether it holds up depends on the chain really failing or surprising, not on a hand-laid sequence that always runs.
